glossary.def: Break: a debuff that lowers the target's DMG Rate for a couple of rounds. Lowers the target's DMG Rate for a couple of rounds, softening its output.

Specialized Berserk: the first strike adds a large chunk of Berserk DMG scaled off Max HP. It grants a state where the first strike deals extra Berserk DMG equal to about 50 percent of the granter's Max HP, and CAN crit. Lasts the whole battle or one round depending on the source. It is a damage type that [Evasion] can pin to 1.

Specialized Guard: a shield layer that removes damage, stacking with extra-HP effects. The shield scales off ATK, removes incoming damage, and stacks with extra-HP effects; total damage removed is capped at 15 times original HP. It is eaten before real HP and can be replenished from DoT dealt to enemies.
Converts excess HP from healing and draining into an equivalent Life Shield, up to a cap based on original HP.
Life Shield: a shield formed from drained/removed damage, capped at a multiple of HP. Damage drained/removed is converted into a shield, capped at a multiple of HP.

Paralysis: locks all of the target's follow-up abilities (Follow-up, Continuous Follow-up, Combo Follow-up). It does not block the main action or Ultimate — it only DISABLES the target's off-turn follow-up attacks, so it hard-counters follow-up-centric teams. Removed by skills that cleanse [Paralysis].
Adhesion: a sticky bind debuff; some skills strip it from themselves and allies. A bind that sticks to a unit; cleanse/immunity skills strip it from self and allies.

Combo Follow-up: a follow-up fired after an ally acts, repeating the Ultimate and unaffected by Hit/Resist. After any ally acts, the unit (and sometimes the whole row) fires 100 percent of the Ultimate's damage and effect at random targets, usually unaffected by Hit/Resist, capped per round. Blocked by follow-up locks.

glossary.def: Internal Injury: a delayed damage seed placed on a target that triggers WHEN the target attacks or is hit. It does no damage on application: it waits, then when the target is hit (or acts) it adds damage equal to a percentage of the caster's ATK, and disappears after triggering once. Several units can 'detonate' or absorb Internal Injury for extra burst.

Evade: a chance to reduce a Direct, Extra, Charge or Berserk hit to just 1 point of damage. On a successful evade the hit is NOT zeroed — it is pinned to exactly 1 damage. It only affects those 4 damage types (it does not block DoT or Injury). Many units carry a bonus when Evade triggers, such as healing or an extra strike.

glossary.def: Unyielding: cannot be reduced below 1 HP — survives an otherwise lethal hit. A FLAG on the unit (the NotDeath family) checked when HP would hit 0 — it lets you SURVIVE rather than shrinking the hit. Some undying states also carry an ignore-damage that pins the hit to 1.

Specialized Guard: a shield layer that removes damage, stacking with extra-HP effects. The shield scales off ATK, removes incoming damage, and stacks with extra-HP effects; total damage removed is capped at 15 times original HP. It is eaten before real HP and can be replenished from DoT dealt to enemies.
Berserk: a state that increases the damage you deal for a number of turns. While active, its bonus ADDS into your amplification sum — so it shares the +300% (×4) amplify ceiling.
Evolve: on hit, immediately cancels the target's [Unyielding] and [Ignore DMG] statuses. On hit it strips the target's [Unyielding] and [Ignore DMG], opening it to damage.

It blocks only non-crit hits; a CRIT forces it to 0, so crit is the answer to this wall. It competes with Evasion inside a max(), does not stack, and is capped at 80 percent.

glossary.def: Crash Bad: a debuff that lowers the target's injury-free (damage-avoid) rate. Lowers the target's injury-free rate so it avoids less damage.

Detonate: the act of setting off a stored effect (Internal Injury, Shatter, Field) into [Detonation] damage. Specialized Guard: a shield layer that removes damage, stacking with extra-HP effects. Stun: the target cannot act for a number of turns. A CONTROL effect, deals no damage. Many stuns are explicitly 'not affected by Hit' — bypassing both Hit and Effect Resist.

Specialized Stun: the Specialized (特化) variant of Stun — the target cannot act and it is harder to remove. glossary.def: A high-tier speed buff that triggers for same-row allies when the caster's speed is high enough.
A debuff applied to all enemies when their Energy drops, denying or disrupting their Energy so they cannot power ultimates.

Encourage: grants allies extra energy at the start of each round for a number of rounds. At the start of each round, allies gain an extra 2 (or 3) energy, lasting 3 to 5 rounds. It is the team's energy accelerator, enabling earlier Ultimates — the counterweight to energy-seal and drain effects.

Specialized Burn: the Specialized (特化) variant of Burn — a DoT that spreads from target to target. Deals damage-over-time scaled off ATK. After any character acts it TRANSFERS to a random target and disappears after 3 transfers; when transferring it prefers targets NOT in an [Unyielding] state, and can also move onto [Revived] and [Resurrected] characters. It stacks up to 6 times. It IS affected by Effect Hit and Effect Resist, and by the Formal Set; but it is NOT affected by [Evade]. In addition, M.Choze and Vaccine Man can deal extra bonus damage from it.

Specialized Acceleration: sharply raises SPD; if the main target is slower, it deals bonus Extra DMG. At battle start it raises SPD by about 20 to 32 percent; if the main target's SPD is LOWER than the unit, it deals an extra 500 to 600 percent ATK as Extra DMG. Higher SPD means acting and ultimate-ing first — the backbone of speed teams.

Evasion: a chance to make Direct, Extra, Charge and Berserk DMG deal only 1 point. Same mechanic as [Evade]: a successful evade pins the hit to 1 damage rather than 0, and only affects those 4 damage types. It is a percentage state granted to the unit, often permanent for the whole battle.

glossary.def: Field: an effect placed on enemies that stores DoT and can be [Detonate]d for a burst. It seeds a DoT onto enemies; several units then 'detonate' all enemy [Fields], converting the original damage into 100 percent [Detonation] damage at once. It is the build-then-burst link of field-based teams.

Ultimate Follow-up: an off-turn follow-up that repeats the Ultimate's damage and effect, at no energy cost. Deals about 70 to 100 percent of the Ultimate skill's damage AND effect, at no energy cost, capped at 2 to 3 times per round. Blocked by [Lock]/[Paralysis]/[Stuck] which lock follow-ups.

Specialized Guard: a shield layer that removes damage, stacking with extra-HP effects. The shield scales off ATK, removes incoming damage, and stacks with extra-HP effects; total damage removed is capped at 15 times original HP. It is eaten before real HP and can be replenished from DoT dealt to enemies.

Detonation: original damage instantly converted into a percentage-based burst — usually from a built-up [Field] or [Shatter]. Not a debuff on the target but a 'detonate' action: it takes stored damage (Field, Shatter) and converts it into 100 percent [Detonation] damage at once. It cannot be [Evaded] the usual way.
Stun/Specialized Stun: refers to [Stun] or its Specialized variant; immunity/removal here covers both. Used when a skill grants immunity to or removes both plain [Stun] and [Specialized Stun].
Stun: the target cannot act for a number of turns. A CONTROL effect, deals no damage. Many stuns are explicitly 'not affected by Hit' — bypassing both Hit and Effect Resist.

Specialized Stun: the Specialized (特化) variant of Stun — the target cannot act and it is harder to remove. Makes the target unable to act, like Stun but sturdier: it is NOT affected by several ordinary immunities and only cleansers that name [Specialized Stun] can remove it. It is a key control tool in high-level arena.

glossary.def: A survival state that keeps the holder alive by drastically reducing incoming DMG (e.g. taking only 20% of it).

Specialized DMG Reflect: reduces incoming Direct and Extra DMG while reflecting a share back to the attacker. Both a mitigation and a counter: it reduces incoming Direct and Extra DMG (usually 40 to 60 percent) and reflects that same share back to the attacker, lasting the whole battle. An enemy can NEGATE it with an anti-reflect skill.

Specialized Berserk: the first strike adds a large chunk of Berserk DMG scaled off Max HP. It grants a state where the first strike deals extra Berserk DMG equal to about 50 percent of the granter's Max HP, and CAN crit. Lasts the whole battle or one round depending on the source. It is a damage type that [Evasion] can pin to 1.

glossary.def: Mê Hoặc (Charm): một trạng thái khống chế khiến mục tiêu quay ra tấn công phe mình hoặc rời trận. Ở bậc Chuyên Biệt, mục tiêu lập tức thoát khỏi giao tranh, dùng một kỹ năng đặc biệt đánh một đồng minh ngẫu nhiên của chính nó, rồi trở lại. Một số nhân vật có [Charm Immunity] hoặc miễn nhiễm [Charm]/[Specialized Charm].

Stun (Choáng): mục tiêu không thể hành động trong số lượt nhất định. Là hiệu ứng KHỐNG CHẾ, không gây sát thương. Nhiều đòn choáng ghi rõ 'không bị ảnh hưởng bởi Hit' — tức bỏ qua cả Hit/Kháng Hiệu Ứng.
Miễn Mê Hoặc: khiến đơn vị miễn nhiễm [Charm]. Cho đơn vị miễn [Charm] trong một thời gian hoặc khi vào trận.

glossary.def: Charm: a control state that turns the target against its own side or forces it off battle. At the Specialized tier the target immediately disengages, uses a special skill to attack a random ally of its own, then returns. Some units have [Charm Immunity] or are immune to [Charm]/[Specialized Charm].
Stun: the target cannot act for a number of turns. A CONTROL effect, deals no damage. Many stuns are explicitly 'not affected by Hit' — bypassing both Hit and Effect Resist.
Charm Immunity: makes the unit immune to [Charm]. Grants a unit immunity to [Charm] for a duration or on entry.

Paralysis: locks all of the target's follow-up abilities (Follow-up, Continuous Follow-up, Combo Follow-up). It does not block the main action or Ultimate — it only DISABLES the target's off-turn follow-up attacks, so it hard-counters follow-up-centric teams. Removed by skills that cleanse [Paralysis].
